subject: Renewal & Rollforward: double reserved capacity and proposed unit rate
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & rollforward — proposal to double reserved capacity (summary + attachments)

Samantha —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our renewal timeline I put together a concise rollforward proposal so Novus can move from your current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU reserved pool starting at contract renewal. Attached are a short SOW and a pricing schedule (spreadsheet) with the proposed new per-hour reserved rate and the term options. High-level summary below: 

- Current: 16 reserved GPUs (monthly reserve) at $2.40 / GPU-hour (12m term)
- Proposal: 32 reserved GPUs (12m term) at $1.95 / GPU-hour (volume-discounted rate)
- Commitment: 12-month reserved term, billing monthly; optional mid-term scaling windows at month 6 and month 9
- Throughput/guarantees: per-pool baseline throughput SLA (see SOW) with 99.95% reserved capacity availability; burst to shared hosted pool for overflow (soft cap)
- Credits: service credits for availability breaches; onboarding support included (2-week carveout for migration tests)

We included two pricing rows in the spreadsheet: (A) the 1.95/hr baseline for the full 32-GPU commit and (B) a staged ramp where Novus starts with 24 reserved GPUs for first 30 days at $1.99/hr then moves to 32 at $1.95/hr. The staged option exists if you prefer lower immediate spend during cutover.

Ask: can you confirm Novus' preferred billing cadence and whether procurement needs any additional artifacts (SOC 2 attestation, network architecture diagram, standard purchase order template)? If useful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our Solutions Engineer to walk the throughput guarantees and runbook for failover to hosted capacity.

Attachments: Novus_SOW_v2.pdf, 32GPU_pricing_schedule.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into contract next week.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Green <samantha@novusai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, procurement@novusai.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & rollforward — proposal to double reserved capacity (summary + attachments)

Diego —

Appreciate the clear summary and the two ramp options. A couple quick questions from my side and procurement (copied):

1) Can you provide a short explanation of how the burst path into hosted capacity works? We need to understand throttling behaviour and any cost exposure for overflow traffic.
2) What uptime credit do you offer if reserved capacity falls below baseline for more than 4 hours in any given month?
3) For the staged ramp option, is there any pricing protection if we decide to accelerate to 32 GPUs after 14 days?

Also cc'ing Raj in procurement — Raj, Diego included SOC2 and the SOW; can you confirm if you need anything else to issue an LOI?

Thanks,
Samantha Green
Director, Platform Engineering
Novus AI

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & rollforward — proposal to double reserved capacity (technical + SLA details)

Samantha / Raj —

Quick answers to your numbered items and a little more color so procurement has what it needs: 

1) Burst path behavior: reserved GPUs are isolated to your dedicated pool and handle baseline traffic. When utilization exceeds the baseline pool capacity (e.g., sustained >95% utilization per GPU for >2 minutes), new requests are routed to our hosted overflow cluster. Overflow usage gets metered at our standard on-demand hosted rate, but we provide a configurable soft-burst allowance that is included in the reserved commitment (we included a 12-hour monthly burst allowance in the SOW for free during the first 90 days of the new term to ease migration). You can cap bursting at any time via routing policies in the Console to avoid surprise spend.

2) Availability credits: for reserved capacity we offer 99.95% monthly availability. If availability for the reserved pool drops below 99.95% we provide service credits on a graduated scale: 99.8–99.95% = 5% of monthly reserved fees, 99.0–99.79% = 15%, <99.0% = 30% (full table in SOW). In practice, most infra incidents are handled with automatic failover to the hosted cluster to maintain request continuity; the credits are for economic remediation.

3) Staged ramp acceleration: you can accelerate from the staged 24->32 plan to full 32 GPUs at any time; we will apply the 32-GPU rate retroactively to the start of the billing period in which you accelerate (i.e., you will be billed the staged price for days prior to acceleration and the 32-GPU rate thereafter). The protective pricing floor is the same quoted $1.95/hr for the 32-GPU commitment — we will not increase that price if you accelerate.

Docs enclosed for procurement: SOC2 report link (embedded in SOW) and a short network architecture diagram. For legal/contract: I attached an RDW amendment link we can push into DocuSign once commercial terms are agreed.

If procurement wants, I can set up a 20–30 minute session tomorrow with our Solutions Engineer (Dev is cc'd) to walk the burst mechanics and routing policy UI.

Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj@novusai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Samantha Green <samantha@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & rollforward — commercial counterproposal

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the details. We are aligned on the technical answers but procurement pushed back on the commercials. Their counter: $1.85 / GPU-hour for the full 32-GPU commit with a one-month credit applied to the first invoice to help smooth Q3 spend. They can commit to signing a 12-month amendment with the payment terms we discussed if you can meet $1.85/hr and the one-month credit.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has flexibility there? Novus is a strategic customer for our ML platform and the certainty around this capacity expansion is important for their roadmap. If we can land around $1.88–1.85/hr with a short-term credit they can push this through legal and finance quickly.

Raj
Director, Procurement — Novus AI

Subject: Re: Renewal & rollforward — commercial counterproposal

Raj / Samantha —

Thanks for the candid counter — I took this to our commercial lead (Marissa) and finance. Good news: we can accept $1.88 / GPU-hour for the 32-GPU reserved commitment with a one-month credit applied to the first invoice. Conditions: 12-month commitment, standard payment terms (30 days net), and inclusion of the 12-hour monthly burst allowance for the first 90 days as described in the SOW. We will prepare an amended commercial schedule and push the DocuSign link to you by EOD.

If that works, I'll queue the amendment for signature and loop in our onboarding PM to schedule the migration tests.

Thanks — excited to scale Novus' capacity with you.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
